reconciliation.policy: Each cell reports the configuration that generated its released rollouts, not one global default per method: every acceleration method was swept per (backbone, embodiment, track) because the attainable operating point depends on that cell's attention share and sequence length. A value departing from the method's modal value is therefore expected, and is accepted when the sweep that chose it is recorded either in the run script or in the matching insights rule.
reconciliation.divergent_but_documented: 125 of 151 divergences carry a recorded sweep and are reported as deliberate per-cell operating points.
reconciliation.divergent_and_undocumented: 26 divergences have no recorded sweep. All of them fall in (cell, method-family) combinations for which no insights rule exists: ctrlworld/single_arm/multiview/cache; dreamdojo/bimanual/singleview/cache; dreamdojo/humanoid/singleview/cache; dreamgen/humanoid/singleview/token; dreamgen/single_arm/multiview/cache; dreamgen/single_arm/multiview/token; dreamgen/single_arm/singleview/cache. Their values were therefore inherited rather than measured on that cell, which the appendix discloses instead of presenting them as tuned optima.
reconciliation.naming: The same knob is spelled differently across backbones (for example PISA_START_LAYER on the Ctrl-World wrappers versus PISA_START_LAYER_IDX on the DiT wrappers, and *_FIRST_LAYERS_FP versus *_START_LAYER_IDX, which express the identical quantity). All spellings are mapped onto one canonical parameter so that a column means the same thing over its whole length; the raw environment names are retained per row for reproducibility.
reconciliation.runnable_but_not_released: 6 cells have a working run script but zero released rollouts (SiTo and ITM on DreamDojo, FasterCache on Ctrl-World). They are printed as not-run rather than omitted, so that an absent result is never mistaken for a negative one.
